passage: Note for Damini's parents, craft hour. I drew a sample card on the board: one flower, five petals, a green stem. Damini studied it, then copied it stroke by stroke, counting petals under her breath. She did not stop there. In the corner she added a big orange sun with long rays, because, she said, her flower needed daylight. Vaibhav, at her table, asked if he could copy her sun. I said yes, and reminded him to give his own card something new. Tomorrow we colour the cards and Damini will write the name inside.

qa.q: What did the teacher draw on the board as the sample card?
qa.a: One flower with five petals and a green stem.

qa.q: What might Damini have been feeling when she added the big orange sun?
qa.a: She was probably pleased with her own idea. She gave a reason, that the flower needed daylight, which shows she wanted the card to be hers. 🙂

qa.q: What other approach could Damini try if she wanted a card that looks less like the sample, and why?
qa.a: She could sketch a few ideas on scrap paper first. Seeing different flowers side by side would help her pick one that suits the birthday child.

qa.q: How might Vaibhav see Damini's card?
qa.a: He sees a sun he would like to borrow, and her changes show him it is fine to copy a starting point and then add something new.

grounding: The child copies the teacher's flower sample and then adds her own sun, so the copy becomes a starting point.

passage: Lavanya's Nani would turn seventy on Sunday, and at the village anganwadi the teacher pinned up a sample card: a pink flower on a tall stem. Lavanya chewed her crayon. Hrithik, beside her, was already drawing a tractor. First she drew a round middle, just like the sample. Then she counted the petals on the wall with her finger and drew the same number. Then came the stem, long and green. She looked at it, frowned, and added a big yellow sun in the corner, rays and all. "Nani likes sun," she told Hrithik. Hrithik nodded and put a sun over his tractor too.

qa.q: What did Lavanya add in the corner of her card?
qa.a: She added a big yellow sun in the corner, rays and all.

qa.q: Why did Lavanya frown and then add the sun?
qa.a: She seemed unsatisfied with a card that only matched the sample and wanted it to feel like her own gift for Nani; she looked pleased once the sun was there.

qa.q: What else could Lavanya try if she wants a card that looks less like everyone else's?
qa.a: She could try a doodle of her own on scrap paper first, or ask the teacher how to draw something Nani loves; copying gave her a start, and those could make it even more personal.

qa.q: How might Hrithik see Lavanya's idea?
qa.a: Hrithik liked the sun enough to put one over his own tractor, so her change gave him a new idea too.

grounding: Shows a child copying the teacher's sample flower step by step and then changing it by adding her own sun.

passage: It was raining in Lisbon, and the kindergarten smelled of wet coats. Abebe's birthday was tomorrow, so Ms Duarte put a sample card on each table: a red flower on a thin stem. Valentina pressed her nose close to it. Step one: a red circle. Step two: petals, one, two, three, four, five, all touching the circle. Step three: the stem. It looked just like the teacher's, and that was a little boring. So she grabbed orange and drew a sun with a smiley face above the flower. "Abebe's sun," she whispered, and slid the card into her bag before anyone could see.

qa.q: Where did Ms Duarte put the sample cards?
qa.a: Ms Duarte put a sample card on each table.

qa.q: What does Valentina's whisper and hiding the card suggest she felt?
qa.a: She seemed proud of her own smiley sun and excited to keep the card a surprise for Abebe's birthday.

qa.q: Which approach might suit Valentina if she wants a card that looks nothing like the sample next time?
qa.a: She could picture her own design first or try a few doodles on scrap paper; the sample was a good start because she changed it.

qa.q: What might it be like for Abebe to get this card?
qa.a: Abebe would get a flower like everyone's, but with a sun made just for this birthday, so it might feel more personal than a plain copy 😊

grounding: Illustrates copying a teacher's sample flower as a starting point and then changing it by adding a personal sun.
